chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any woman who goes out from her house without the permission of her husband, there is no maintenance (nafaqah) for her until she returns.'

key_terms.نَفَقَة: Maintenance/financial support provided to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's right to maintenance if she leaves home without her husband's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of 'nushuz' (disobedience) in Shia jurisprudence, linking a wife's physical absence from the marital home without permission to the suspension of her financial rights (nafaqah). It reflects the scholarly view that while obedience is obligatory, it is conditional upon the husband's provision, creating a reciprocal legal framework. The ruling highlights the domestic sphere as the primary context for marital duties, a key theme in fiqh al-mara'ah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whichever woman goes out from her house without a permission of her husband, so there are no expenses for her until she returns’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Any woman who goes out of her house without the permission of her husband loses her right of maintenance until she comes back.’”
